links.reason: Both set the wife against the common woman, and Paripadal 64-65 even matches Naladiyar's பன்மார்பு with its own chest question (நின் மார்பும் ... ஓர் ஒத்த நீர்மைய கொல்). That is the same situation from two sides rather than one poem answering the other: 303 asks whether he holds her suffering in his heart (நெஞ்சத்தானே), not whether he is awake.

The tie is real and specific: both liken the woman to விராஅன் இருப்பை (கைவண் விராஅன் / தேர் வண் விராஅன்). The difference the pair teaches is in the Tamil.

Both verses group theft, gambling and bad company (20: கள்ளான், கழுமான், கரியாரை நள்ளான்; 27: புறன்நட்டான் ... கள்களவு சூது), and 27 does present the vices as picked up through company. But both texts are corrupt and the construal of each is uncertain, so the causal claim rests on a reconstruction.
links.text_issue: Sirupanchamoolam 20 line 1 கள்ளான்கு தென்றும் is corrupt (read as கள்ளான் சூது என்றும்); 27 lines 2-4 are hard to divide.

links.reason: The note says both carry the thurai of disputing the season, but Kuruntokai 66's colophon gives only தோழி கூற்று; only Natrinai 274 has பருவம் மாறுபட்டது. Ainkurunuru 112's last line, மறந்தோம் மன்ற நாணுடை நெஞ்சே, was repaired, and it does not say what was forgotten. Making it 'we have forgotten our modesty' to match Kural 1257's நாணென ஒன்றோ அறியலம் picks one sense the Tamil does not fix.
links.text_issue: Ainkurunuru 112 line 4 was repaired from a damaged reading.

links.reason: Both akam poems by different poets (Kapilar, Paranar) measure the woman's scent by the kaanthal of Nalli's slopes (238 நள்ளி ... அடுக்கத்து ... காந்தள் ... நாறும் நறு நுதல்; 152 நள்ளி சோலை அடுக்கத்து ... கடவுட் காந்தள் ... நாறி). A patron's name carried into the image in two hands is a specific, real connection.

The echo of துணை is real: Kural 1263 உள்ளம் துணையாகச் சென்றார், Ainkurunuru 496 தோள்துணை யாக வந்தனர். But the 'reproach that he chose resolve over her' is Parimelazhagar's gloss, not the couplet's words, and a shared word in going and returning is better called a shared image than a qualification.

Both make the announcement itself the injury: the couplet's பிரிவுரைக்கும் வன்கண்ணர், the poem's செல்வல் என்ப set directly against her fading (ஆய்கவின் தொலைய ... பசப்ப). The couplet judges the speaker while the poem shows the body changing, which is a specific difference.

links.text_issue: Ainkurunuru 358 line 4 உடிஅத்தெழு looks corrupt (perhaps உடைத்தெழு).

links.reason: The formula is verbatim (விழுத்தொடை மறவர் வில்லிட/வில்இட ... எழுத்துடை நடுகல்). In Akananuru 53 it marks the road he took for wealth (பொருளே காதலர் காதல்); in 352 it is part of the road he crossed home without calling it hard (வெஞ்சுரம் அரிய என்னார் வந்தனர்). The opposite uses are in the Tamil.

Ainkurunuru 14 praises the chest's softness (பனித்துயில் செய்யும் இன்சாயற்றே) and Naladiyar 389 shows the chest smeared by other women. Apart from the shared word for chest there is no link, and 'the later moralist turns the older image' invents a dependence the verses do not show; the marked chest is already common in the Sangam corpus itself.

Both find union sweet after sulking: Kural 1330 ஊடுதல் ... அதற்கின்பம் கூடி முயங்கப் பெறின், Ainthinai Aimpathu 30 ஊடி யிருப்பினும் ... கூடல் இனிதாம். ஊடி யிருப்பினும் can just as well mean 'though I have sulked', so the claimed collapse of the Kural's sequence is a fine distinction the Tamil does not force; they largely agree.

The garland as evidence is a real point of contact: Kural 1313 கோட்டுப் பூச் சூடினும் காயும், Kalittokai 88 ஒள் இதழ் சோர்ந்த நின் கண்ணியும் with nail and tooth marks. But the couplet belongs to a lovers' quarrel with no straying husband, so saying its complaint 'rests on' the marutham scene claims a dependence the verses do not show.

Gladness at guests is shared (Kural 84 முகனமர்ந்து நல்விருந்து ஓம்புவான்; Natrinai 142 அல்லில் ஆயினும் விருந்து வரின் உவக்கும்), and the night detail is a real addition. But the poem's பொய்யா யாணர் is the woodland's plenty, not the reward the Kural promises, so the third claim in 'teaches' is a stretch.

Both refuse the bard with the nursing body set against the women of the street (Natrinai 380 புதல்வற் புல்லிப் புனிறு நாறும் ... வால் இழை மகளிர் சேரி; Ainthinai Ezhupathu 47 புதல்வன் உண ... வருமுலையார் சேரி). Same poet, same decade: 82's கொளக்கொளக் குறையாச் செல்வம் becomes in 90 the stated ground of a simile, கொளக்குறை படாமையின் முந்நீர் அனையை, beside ஈரம் உடைமையின் and அளப்பருமையின். The observation about the ground preceding the simile is specific and true.
links.text_issue: Patitruppattu 90 line 16 prints முந்நர்ண for முந்நீர்.

links.reason: Kalittokai 61 has the friend say நாண் இலன் மன்ற இவன் and the man threaten the madal (பல்லார் நக்கு எள்ளப்படு மடல்மா ஏறி); Kural 1133 is the man's own loss of நாண் to the madal. The poem's close (வரூஉம் ... குறித்தது கொள்ளாது போகாக் குணன் உடையன்) supports 'what persuades her', so the two vantages are real.

Ainkurunuru 410 says the hour ஒத்தன்று ... பாணனது யாழே: the bard's lute was in accord with that joyful hour, not that it fell short of it. And 402 is itself the family scene (புதல்வற் கவைஇய தாய்புற முயங்கி), so ranking the child above the couple misdescribes both verses.

The ஒருநாள arithmetic is shared (271 ஒருநாள் ... தவப்பன்னாள்; 280 ஒருநாள் புணரப் புணரின் அரைநாள் வாழ்க்கையும் வேண்டலென்). But the two are not incompatible: both price the single day very high, one speaker in advance and one after. Kuruntokai 271's colophon thinai is marutham, not kurinji.

Malaipadukadam 302-304 has hill wives sing over tiger wounds on their husbands' chests as காப்பு, and Purananuru 281 calls for காஞ்சி பாடி ... காக்கம் over a warrior's wound. A specific rite appears in both a war and a hunting setting, which supports the teaches sentence.

Kural 1155 is about the husband's departure on a journey (பிரிவோம்பல் ... நீங்கின் அரிதால் புணர்வு), while Ainkurunuru 228 fears the lover leaving with his suit unspoken (இரந்துகுறை யுறாஅன் பெயரின்). The 'mechanism' that the man's suit must pass through the friend is the marker's kalavu frame placed on a couplet that has none; it is only the shared fear of his leaving.

The same poet, in adjoining decades, uses the same charge: அறனில் யாய் (385) and அறனில் பாலே (376). The mother blames the fate that joined and sent the girl (போக்கிய புணர்த்த), the daughter blames the mother, which is a real, defensible conflict over whether the going was right. The gloss of என்கெடுத்து இருந்த as 'kept her at home' is not certain.

The வேல்/கோல் pair is genuinely shared: Kural 546 வேலன்று வென்றி தருவது ... கோல், and the idyll's வேலினும் வெய்ய கானம் ... கோலினுந் தண்ணிய ... தோளே. The contrast in ranking is true, but 'an older fixed figure that the Kural argued with' is a historical claim two verses cannot carry.

The bell and the birds are inverted across the two: in Akananuru 4 the man ties the bell-tongues so as not to startle the paired birds (துணையொடு வதிந்த தாதுண் பறவை பேதுறல் அஞ்சி மணிநா ஆர்த்த), and in the venba she takes the birds' noise for the bells (மணிஅரவம் ... புள்ளரவம்). Calling 50 a secret-love poem is not in the Tamil, but the central claim holds.

Kural 805 excuses a friend's hurtful act by பெருங்கிழமை, and the heroine of 167 excuses the unkept promise (நல்குவன் போலக் கூறி நல்கான்) by தொல் கேள். The pair shows a specific rule of friendship working inside love, and the cost it puts on the wronged side.

Both turn on an oath made before the friend: 227 asks whether the friend has let go the oath he swore (நீ விட்டனையோ அவர் உற்ற சூளே); 358 asks the god not to harm him though he gave assurances to the friend (நின்னொடு தெளித்தனர் ஆயினும் ... அணங்கல் ஓம்புமதி). Wanting the oath kept and fearing its punishment are the two halves.

Both are Paranar's and name Minjili and Ori's Kolli in a measure of the woman (265 மிஞிலி காக்கும் பாரத்து அன்ன ... ஓரி கொல்லிக் கலி மயில்; 208 மிஞிலியொடு ... பாழிப் பறந்தலை ... ஓரி ... கொல்லிக் கார்மலர்). The longer poem gives the battle behind the name, so the shorter poem's name carries war fame. That is the puram-name connection done well.

Both lodge the lover in the heart: Kural 1249 உள்ளத்தார் காதலவரால் ... யாருழைச் சேறி, Kuruntokai 228 நெடுஞ்சேண் ணாட்டார் ஆயினும் நெஞ்சிற்கு அணியர். The couplet uses it to rebuke the heart and the poem to cancel distance, which is a real difference of treatment.

The friend's false-season argument is offered and stands in Kuruntokai 382 (வம்புப் பெய்யுமால் மழையே ... வாராரோ), and in Thinaimalai 103 it is reported (பருவந்தான் பட்டின்றே என்றி) and met with அட்டினேன் ஆவி. Lines 1-2 of the venba are obscure, but the received-and-failing half is clear.

The shared phrase is real (Pattinappalai 249 கந்துடைப் பொதியில் ... பலர்தொழ; Thirumurugatruppadai 226 பொதியிலும் கந்துடை நிலையினும), and the pair confirms the post-hall as a place of worship. But 'measured against the Murugan poem' is the reader's juxtaposition, and the claim reduces to a shared institution.

Both set the sleepless woman against a sleeping world (Kural 1168 மன்னுயிர் எல்லாம் துயிற்றி; Natrinai 303 பாக்கம் துயில் மடிந்தன்றே), and the crying paired anril (துணை புணர் அன்றில்) is a real addition. But 303's question is whether he knows her suffering (நம்வயின் வருந்தும் நன்னுதல் என்பது உண்டுகொல் ... நெஞ்சத்தானே), not whether he lies awake.

The herdsman's flute at dusk is the shared mullai convention. Ezhupathu 22 is not without feeling: it closes on முழங்கிவில் கோலிற்று வான், the sky drawing its bow, an arming image close to Aimpathu 7's வேல்கொண்டு எறிவது. 'Relies on it unstated' misses this, and the teaches sentence restates the convention.

The heron as the only witness of the secret oath appears in both: Kuruntokai 25 யாரும் இல்லை ... குருகும் உண்டு, its eyes on the aaral fish, against Ainthinai Aimpathu 45 மன்ற விடுவனவோ ... குருகு. On the plain reading one witness is useless and the other is trusted to hold the oath, so the tension is defensible and the teaches sentence is specific.

The wording is near-identical: Naladiyar 370 மாரி அறவே அறுமே ... வாரி அறவே அறும் and Valayapathi 51 வாரி பெருகப் பெருகிய ... வாரி சுருங்க ... மாரி பெருகப் பெருகி அறவறும். The fragment does add the rise to the fall, so the teaches sentence is precise.

poems.note: The sea's sleeplessness is joined to her by எம்போல், so its sense is stated, not implied.
The season is openly made the messenger (தூது வந்தன்றே); its flowers are open similes.
Otter = the man, the vaalai taken as daily food = the women he takes; the situation (his other women) is in the thurai இற்பரத்தை கூற்று.

iraicchi.act: the calf of the newly calved buffalo sleeps on by its mother at the rich house
iraicchi.sense: the daughter who should have stayed by her mother has gone off across the waste

poems.note: An excerpt of a long poem: the peacock drunk on honey it took for water suggests the girl, but no second correspondence is drawn in these lines.

iraicchi.act: the tusker bends down sugarcane for its pregnant mate's craving
iraicchi.sense: the man of that hill will cherish and provide for the woman, as the song's 'I will not leave my own' says of him

poems.note: Each stanza pairs a hill image with a stated quality of the man; only the elephant stanza is an act of one creature for its mate.

iraicchi.act: the bat flies at evening to the fruiting tree
iraicchi.sense: every creature goes to its place of pleasure at dusk, while the man who left her alone stays away

iraicchi.act: the kadamba blossom smells sweet so that travellers think of those left behind
iraicchi.sense: on that road even the flowers should make him remember her and turn home

iraicchi.act: the peacock dances though no rain has come
iraicchi.sense: he goes on loving her though she gives him no grace

poems.note: The crab is addressed, not used to carry a sense.
The crab leaving the mud for its hole may stand for the man, but line 4 is too unclear to name a second correspondence.

Boar raiding the guarded millet = the man coming for the guarded girl; the hunter's ambush at the narrow pass = the danger and watch on the night path; the meat shared by kin = discovery by the family.

iraicchi.act: the male crow searches the pool for ayirai fish for its heavily pregnant mate
iraicchi.sense: the bird provides for its mate while the lord of the shore withholds grace from her

carrier: வாள் வரிக் கடுங் கண் வயப் புலி
iraicchi.act: the tiger lies in wait at the path to end its mate's hunger
iraicchi.sense: the man of that land has not yet rightly claimed and provided for her (உரிதினின் பெறாது)

poems.note: The season's coming against his not coming is stated outright (அவரோ வாரார் தான்வந் தன்றே).
The hunter digging an old pit for tubers who finds a bright gem = the man who came for little and found her; the promise to bring her home is stated.
